author: Pankaj K. Agarwal
title: Truly subquadratic exact Euclidean bipartite matching
text:
Given n red and n blue points with arbitrary real coordinates in the plane, can a minimum-total-Euclidean-length perfect red–blue matching be computed in O(n^{2-epsilon}) time for fixed epsilon>0? Near-linear approximation schemes do not settle exact optimization.

     References:
     Sharathkumar and Agarwal, “A Near-Linear Time epsilon-Approximation Algorithm for Geometric Bipartite Matching,” explicitly asks for subquadratic exact planar Euclidean bipartite matching.
     https://users.cs.duke.edu/~pankaj/publications/papers/eps-match.pdf
     Later authored progress remains on approximation: Agarwal, Raghvendra, Shirzadian and Sowle, “An Improved epsilon-Approximation Algorithm for Geometric Bipartite Matching,” SWAT 2022.
     https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.SWAT.2022.6
     The arbitrary-coordinate Euclidean formulation matters: neither non-bipartite planar matching nor bounded-integer-coordinate variants should be mistaken for this question.
description: Given n red and n blue points with arbitrary real coordinates in the plane, can a minimum-total-Euclidean-length perfect red–blue matching be computed in O(n^{2-epsilon}) time for fixed epsilon>0? Near-linear approximation schemes do not settle exact optimization.

author: Alan M. Frieze
title: Asymptotically optimal algorithms for random three-dimensional assignment
text:
For independent Exp(1) costs C_{i,j,k}, find permutations π,σ minimizing Σ_i C_{i,π(i),σ(i)}. Is there a polynomial-time algorithm whose cost is (1+o(1)) times optimum with high probability, extending the strong algorithmic understanding of two-dimensional random assignment?

     Remark: Status evidence is older: the cited sources pose this question, and the literature check found no resolution by the cutoff.

     References:
     A. Frieze and G. B. Sorkin, Efficient Algorithms for Three-Dimensional Axial and Planar Random Assignment Problems, Random Structures & Algorithms 46(1), 2015. https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.0390
     A. Frieze, Random Structures and Algorithms, survey, open problem P10 (asymptotics and asymptotically optimal heuristics for random multidimensional assignment). https://www.math.cmu.edu/~af1p/Paper.pdf
description: For independent Exp(1) costs C_{i,j,k}, find permutations π,σ minimizing Σ_i C_{i,π(i),σ(i)}. Is there a polynomial-time algorithm whose cost is (1+o(1)) times optimum with high probability, extending the strong algorithmic understanding of two-dimensional random assignment?

author: Alan M. Frieze
title: Polynomial-time exact optimization of random asymmetric TSP
text:
When every directed edge of a complete graph receives an independent uniform[0,1] cost, can the minimum-cost Hamiltonian cycle be found exactly in polynomial time with high probability? Bell–Frieze’s quasipolynomial-time algorithm leaves this central average-case algorithmic question open.

     References:
     T. Bell and A. Frieze, Solving a Random Asymmetric TSP Exactly in Quasi-Polynomial Time w.h.p., preprint first posted 2023, revised December 2025; journal publication 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.02946
     A. Frieze and G. B. Sorkin, The Probabilistic Relationship Between the Assignment and Asymmetric Traveling Salesman Problems, SICOMP. https://doi.org/10.1137/S0097539701391518
description: When every directed edge of a complete graph receives an independent uniform[0,1] cost, can the minimum-cost Hamiltonian cycle be found exactly in polynomial time with high probability? Bell–Frieze’s quasipolynomial-time algorithm leaves this central average-case algorithmic question open.

author: Robert Krauthgamer
title: Size-bounded approximate multicommodity-flow sparsifiers
text:
For every undirected capacitated graph with k terminals and every ε>0, does there exist a graph of size f(k,ε), independent of the original graph’s size and capacities, preserving all terminal multicommodity-flow congestion values within 1+ε? The sparsifier may have new nonterminal vertices and need not be obtained by contraction.

     Remark: Exact preservation is already impossible with size bounded solely by k, even for six terminals. The contraction-only (1+ε) version also has six-terminal obstructions; neither settles unrestricted approximate graph sparsifiers.

     References:
     A. Andoni, A. Gupta and R. Krauthgamer, Towards (1+ε)-Approximate Flow Sparsifiers. https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.3252
     R. Krauthgamer and R. Mosenzon, Exact Flow Sparsification Requires Unbounded Size, SODA 2023. https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07363
     Y. Chen and Z. Tan, On (1+ε)-Approximate Flow Sparsifiers, 2023 research talk abstract. https://theory.cs.northwestern.edu/quarterly-theory-workshop-fall-2023-junior-theorists-workshop/
description: For every undirected capacitated graph with k terminals and every ε>0, does there exist a graph of size f(k,ε), independent of the original graph’s size and capacities, preserving all terminal multicommodity-flow congestion values within 1+ε? The sparsifier may have new nonterminal vertices and need not be obtained by contraction.

author: Claire Mathieu
title: The exact random-order ratio of Best Fit bin packing
text:
An adversary chooses the item multiset, then its order is uniformly randomly permuted before Best Fit packs it. Determine the asymptotic worst-case expected ratio to OPT; the conjectured value near 1.15 is still separated substantially from the upper bound.

     Remark: Beating 3/2 is already resolved: the 2024 result gives 1.5−ε for a fixed ε>0 and a lower bound of 1.144. The open problem here is the true ratio.

     References:
     C. Kenyon (now C. Mathieu), Best-Fit Bin-Packing with Random Order, SODA 1996; publication listed in her CV. https://www.irif.fr/_media/users/claire/cv-complet-mathieu-2018.pdf
     A. Hebbar, A. Khan and K. V. N. Sreenivas, Bin Packing under Random-Order: Breaking the Barrier of 3/2, SODA 2024. https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.04714
description: An adversary chooses the item multiset, then its order is uniformly randomly permuted before Best Fit packs it. Determine the asymptotic worst-case expected ratio to OPT; the conjectured value near 1.15 is still separated substantially from the upper bound.

author: Shiri Chechik
title: Optimal distance oracles that also report paths
text:
For undirected positively weighted graphs, can a path-reporting distance oracle simultaneously achieve O(n^(1+1/k)) space, stretch 2k−1, and O(1) query overhead plus time proportional to the reported path? This asks to match Chechik's distance-only bounds while returning an actual approximate shortest path.

     References:
     S. Chechik and T. Zhang, Path-Reporting Distance Oracles with Logarithmic Stretch and Linear Size, ICALP 2024; obtains stretch 12k and O(log log k) overhead: https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2024.42
description: For undirected positively weighted graphs, can a path-reporting distance oracle simultaneously achieve O(n^(1+1/k)) space, stretch 2k−1, and O(1) query overhead plus time proportional to the reported path? This asks to match Chechik's distance-only bounds while returning an actual approximate shortest path.

author: Liam Roditty
title: Truly subquadratic preprocessing for stretch-3 distance oracles
text:
For every fixed epsilon > 0, can a nonnegatively weighted undirected graph with m=O(n^(2-epsilon)) edges be preprocessed in O(n^(2-delta)) time, for some delta > 0, into a stretch-3 oracle with O(n^(3/2)) space and constant query time? Kadria and Roditty's 2025 work settled the analogous preprocessing question for stretch 2k-1 when k>2, leaving k=2 open.

     References:
     Kadria and Roditty, Faster Algorithms for (2k-1)-Stretch Distance Oracles (July 2025), Problem 1 and discussion: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.06721v1
description: For every fixed epsilon > 0, can a nonnegatively weighted undirected graph with m=O(n^(2-epsilon)) edges be preprocessed in O(n^(2-delta)) time, for some delta > 0, into a stretch-3 oracle with O(n^(3/2)) space and constant query time? Kadria and Roditty's 2025 work settled the analogous preprocessing question for stretch 2k-1 when k>2, leaving k=2 open.

author: Xi Chen
title: The complexity of tolerant monotonicity testing
text:
Determine the query complexity of distinguishing Boolean functions on {0,1}^n that are ε₁-close to monotone from those ε₂-far, for fixed 0<ε₁<ε₂. Even nonadaptive testing has an exponential gap in the exponent between 2^{Ω(n^{1/4})} lower bounds and roughly 2^{Õ(√n)} upper bounds; the power of adaptivity is also unresolved.

     References:
     X. Chen, A. De, Y. Li, S. Nadimpalli and R. A. Servedio, Mildly Exponential Lower Bounds on Tolerant Testers for Monotonicity, Unateness, and Juntas, SODA 2024: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.12513
     D. Ron, Let's Try to Be More Tolerant: On Tolerant Property Testing and Distance Approximation, ICALP 2025: https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol334-icalp2025/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.2/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.2.pdf
description: Determine the query complexity of distinguishing Boolean functions on {0,1}^n that are ε₁-close to monotone from those ε₂-far, for fixed 0<ε₁<ε₂. Even nonadaptive testing has an exponential gap in the exponent between 2^{Ω(n^{1/4})} lower bounds and roughly 2^{Õ(√n)} upper bounds; the power of adaptivity is also unresolved.

author: Xi Chen
title: Efficient black-box testing of high-dimensional convexity
text:
Given membership-query access to S⊆R^n, can convexity versus constant Gaussian-measure distance from every convex set be tested with poly(n) queries? Chen and coauthors prove polynomial query lower bounds, while the general upper bound is 2^{Õ(√n)} for constant accuracy, leaving the basic polynomial-versus-superpolynomial question open.

     References:
     X. Chen, A. De, S. Nadimpalli, R. A. Servedio and E. Waingarten, Lower Bounds for Convexity Testing, SODA 2025: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17958
description: Given membership-query access to S⊆R^n, can convexity versus constant Gaussian-measure distance from every convex set be tested with poly(n) queries? Chen and coauthors prove polynomial query lower bounds, while the general upper bound is 2^{Õ(√n)} for constant accuracy, leaving the basic polynomial-versus-superpolynomial question open.

author: Thomas Sauerwald
title: A general characterization of parallel random-walk cover time
text:
For any connected undirected graph G and k independent lazy random walks with worst-case starting vertices, characterize within constant factors the expected time until their union has visited every vertex. The challenge is a graph-general analogue of single-walk cover-time theory, including the speedup as k varies.

     References:
     Rivera, Sauerwald and Sylvester, Multiple Random Walks on Graphs: Mixing Few to Cover Many, ICALP 2021/CPC 2023: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.07893
description: For any connected undirected graph G and k independent lazy random walks with worst-case starting vertices, characterize within constant factors the expected time until their union has visited every vertex. The challenge is a graph-general analogue of single-walk cover-time theory, including the speedup as k varies.

author: Tomasz Kociumaka
title: Fast constant-factor fully dynamic edit distance
text:
Maintain a constant-factor approximation to edit distance between two strings under arbitrary single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions, using polylogarithmic expected amortized update time after polynomial preprocessing. The known joint work achieves subpolynomial approximation and update time, leaving this stronger combination open.

     Remark: This is an editorial strengthening of their tradeoff; exact algorithms whose update time depends on the current distance do not provide this guarantee for arbitrary strings.

     References:
     Kociumaka, Mukherjee and Saha, Approximating Edit Distance in the Fully Dynamic Model, 2023: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07175
description: Maintain a constant-factor approximation to edit distance between two strings under arbitrary single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions, using polylogarithmic expected amortized update time after polynomial preprocessing. The known joint work achieves subpolynomial approximation and update time, leaving this stronger combination open.

author: Michael T. Goodrich
title: Average-case optimality of standard Shellsort
text:
Is there a fixed, n-dependent increment sequence for standard Shellsort whose expected number of comparisons is O(n log n) on a uniformly random input permutation? Here each increment means fully insertion-sorting the corresponding residue-class subsequences.

     Remark: Goodrich's randomized Shellsort and later Zig-zag Sort already attain O(n log n) for different procedures; they do not settle this standard-Shellsort question. The selection is a historical open problem connected to his work, not an assertion of current activity.

     References:
     Goodrich, Randomized Shellsort: A Simple Data-Oblivious Sorting Algorithm, JACM 58(6), 2011: https://ics.uci.edu/~goodrich/pubs/J-75.pdf
     Sedgewick, Research: Shellsort open problems: https://sedgewick.io/research/
description: Is there a fixed, n-dependent increment sequence for standard Shellsort whose expected number of comparisons is O(n log n) on a uniformly random input permutation? Here each increment means fully insertion-sorting the corresponding residue-class subsequences.

author: Santosh S. Vempala
title: Nearly quadratic oracle complexity for convex-body volume
text:
Can a randomized algorithm estimate the volume of an n-dimensional convex body to fixed relative error using O(n² polylog n) membership queries with success probability at least 2/3? Assume known concentric inner and outer balls with polynomial radius ratio; the goal is the optimal dimension dependence, not the fixed-dimension small-error regime.

     Remark: Editorial target in Vempala’s volume-computation program.

     References:
     Jia, Laddha, Lee and Vempala, Reducing Isotropy and Volume to KLS, STOC 2021: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.02146
     Lee and Vempala, The Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits Conjecture, survey: https://faculty.cc.gatech.edu/~vempala/papers/kls_survey.pdf
description: Can a randomized algorithm estimate the volume of an n-dimensional convex body to fixed relative error using O(n² polylog n) membership queries with success probability at least 2/3? Assume known concentric inner and outer balls with polynomial radius ratio; the goal is the optimal dimension dependence, not the fixed-dimension small-error regime.

author: Kunal Talwar
title: An additive privacy cost for adversarial bandits
text:
For K-armed bandits with an oblivious adversary and central ε-differential privacy, can expected regret match the nonprivate O(√(KT)) term plus a privacy penalty independent of T up to logarithms? Talwar’s joint 2025 algorithm instead has a multiplicative 1/√ε cost, and its lower-bound discussion leaves unrestricted algorithms open.

     References:
     H. Asi, V. Raman and K. Talwar, Faster Rates for Private Adversarial Bandits, ICML 2025, especially Section 5: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.21790
description: For K-armed bandits with an oblivious adversary and central ε-differential privacy, can expected regret match the nonprivate O(√(KT)) term plus a privacy penalty independent of T up to logarithms? Talwar’s joint 2025 algorithm instead has a multiplicative 1/√ε cost, and its lower-bound discussion leaves unrestricted algorithms open.

author: Kunal Talwar
title: Optimal private sample complexity for nonsmooth nonconvex optimization
text:
Determine the optimal sample complexity for polynomial-time (ε,δ)-private algorithms finding approximate Goldstein-stationary points of Lipschitz, nonsmooth, nonconvex population losses with bounded initial suboptimality. The target is a tight dependence on dimension, privacy, neighborhood radius and stationarity error, closing the upper/lower-bound gap in Talwar’s joint 2025 work.

     References:
     G. Kornowski, D. Liu and K. Talwar, Improved Sample Complexity for Private Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization, ICML 2025, Section 8: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05880
description: Determine the optimal sample complexity for polynomial-time (ε,δ)-private algorithms finding approximate Goldstein-stationary points of Lipschitz, nonsmooth, nonconvex population losses with bounded initial suboptimality. The target is a tight dependence on dimension, privacy, neighborhood radius and stationarity error, closing the upper/lower-bound gap in Talwar’s joint 2025 work.

author: Giuseppe F. Italiano
title: Derandomizing the n^{5/2} worst-case dynamic APSP bound
text:
Maintain exact distances in a directed weighted graph under insertion or deletion of a vertex and its incident edges, with constant-time distance queries and Õ(n²) space. Can deterministic worst-case update time match the Õ(n^{5/2}) randomized bound?

     Remark: The Õ(n²) amortized update target and the randomized Õ(n^{5/2}) worst-case target are already achieved. This is the deterministic worst-case strengthening, for graphs with no negative cycles.

     References:
     C. Demetrescu and G. F. Italiano, A New Approach to Dynamic All Pairs Shortest Paths, JACM 2004. https://art.torvergata.it/handle/2108/38550
     X. Mao, Fully-Dynamic All-Pairs Shortest Paths: Likely Optimal Worst-Case Update Time, STOC 2024. https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02662
description: Maintain exact distances in a directed weighted graph under insertion or deletion of a vertex and its incident edges, with constant-time distance queries and Õ(n²) space. Can deterministic worst-case update time match the Õ(n^{5/2}) randomized bound?

author: Giuseppe F. Italiano
title: Deterministic worst-case polylogarithmic dynamic 2-edge-connectivity
text:
Maintain an undirected graph under edge insertions and deletions so that queries ask whether two vertices remain connected after any one edge failure. Can both updates and queries have deterministic polylogarithmic worst-case time?

     Remark: Deterministic polylogarithmic amortized bounds are known; requiring worst-case update bounds is essential. This is a strengthening of Italiano’s dynamic connectivity program.

     References:
     Z. Galil and G. F. Italiano, Fully Dynamic Algorithms for 2-Edge Connectivity, SIAM Journal on Computing 21, 1992. https://doi.org/10.1137/0221062
description: Maintain an undirected graph under edge insertions and deletions so that queries ask whether two vertices remain connected after any one edge failure. Can both updates and queries have deterministic polylogarithmic worst-case time?

author: Christian Wulff-Nilsen
title: Near-linear-space exact planar distance oracles with polylogarithmic queries
text:
Can every weighted directed planar graph admit an exact distance oracle using O(n polylog n) space and polylogarithmic query time, with polynomial preprocessing? Wulff-Nilsen’s exact-oracle work and subsequent tradeoffs leave this combination of space and query bounds unresolved.

     Remark: Linear space and constant query time are known for fixed-error approximate undirected planar distances. The exact-distance requirement is essential; assume nonnegative edge weights.

     References:
     V. Fredslund-Hansen, S. Mozes and C. Wulff-Nilsen, Truly Subquadratic Exact Distance Oracles with Constant Query Time for Planar Graphs, ISAAC 2021. https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.ISAAC.2021.25
     Faster Construction of a Planar Distance Oracle with Õ(1) Query Time, ICALP 2025 (reviews Wulff-Nilsen’s exact-oracle results and the space/query tradeoffs). https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol334-icalp2025/html/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.33/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.33.html
description: Can every weighted directed planar graph admit an exact distance oracle using O(n polylog n) space and polylogarithmic query time, with polynomial preprocessing? Wulff-Nilsen’s exact-oracle work and subsequent tradeoffs leave this combination of space and query bounds unresolved.

author: Seshadhri Comandur
title: Polynomial accuracy dependence for sublinear LIS estimation
text:
With adaptive random access to an array of length n, can its longest increasing subsequence length be estimated to additive error εn in time polynomial in log n and 1/ε? Saks and Seshadhri achieved polylogarithmic dependence on n but exponential dependence on inverse accuracy.

     Remark: This is an editorial continuation of Saks–Seshadhri. Adaptivity is essential: known nonadaptive lower bounds rule out the stated polynomial dependence simultaneously on log n and 1/ε.

     References:
     Saks and Seshadhri, Estimating the Longest Increasing Sequence in Polylogarithmic Time, SIAM Journal on Computing (2017): https://doi.org/10.1137/130942152
     Andoni, Nosatzki, Sinha and Stein, Estimating the Longest Increasing Subsequence in Nearly Optimal Time, FOCS (2022), introduction: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.05106
     Newman and Varma, New Sublinear Algorithms and Lower Bounds for LIS Estimation, ICALP (2021), nonadaptive lower bound: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.05805
description: With adaptive random access to an array of length n, can its longest increasing subsequence length be estimated to additive error εn in time polynomial in log n and 1/ε? Saks and Seshadhri achieved polylogarithmic dependence on n but exponential dependence on inverse accuracy.

author: Yuichi Yoshida
title: Estimating sparse finite-field matrix rank with sublinear queries
text:
For n×n matrices over F₂ with O(1) nonzeros in every row and column, how many row/column adjacency queries are needed to estimate rank within additive εn? Yoshida conjectured that Ω(n) queries are necessary in general, despite efficient special cases corresponding to graph incidence matrices.

     References:
     Yoshida, Approximating Rank in the Bounded-Degree Model, Open Problems in Sublinear Algorithms, Problem 68 (2014): https://sublinear.info/68
description: For n×n matrices over F₂ with O(1) nonzeros in every row and column, how many row/column adjacency queries are needed to estimate rank within additive εn? Yoshida conjectured that Ω(n) queries are necessary in general, despite efficient special cases corresponding to graph incidence matrices.

author: Gary L. Miller
title: Truly linear-time Laplacian solving
text:
Can a weighted graph Laplacian system Lx=b be solved to a fixed relative error, such as 1/10 in the L-energy norm, in expected O(m) arithmetic operations for an m-edge connected graph? This asks to remove the remaining logarithmic overhead from Miller’s line of nearly linear solvers.

     Remark: The question assumes sum(b)=0 and measures relative error against the exact solution modulo the Laplacian nullspace; it concerns arithmetic complexity, not bit complexity.

     References:
     Koutis, Miller and Peng, A nearly-m log n time solver for SDD linear systems (2011), https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.4842
     Cohen, Kyng, Miller, Pachocki, Peng, Rao and Xu, Solving SDD Linear Systems in Nearly m log^{1/2} n Time (2014), https://doi.org/10.1145/2591796.2591833
description: Can a weighted graph Laplacian system Lx=b be solved to a fixed relative error, such as 1/10 in the L-energy norm, in expected O(m) arithmetic operations for an m-edge connected graph? This asks to remove the remaining logarithmic overhead from Miller’s line of nearly linear solvers.

author: Kasper Green Larsen
title: Polynomial lower bounds for adaptive dynamic data structures
text:
Exhibit an explicit dynamic Boolean data-structure problem with O(log n)-bit operation arguments for which every polynomial-space adaptive cell-probe structure, with Θ(log n)-bit cells, requires n^{Ω(1)} update or query cost. Achieving such an unconditional bound would go far beyond Larsen’s polylogarithmic lower bounds without restricting adaptivity.

     Remark: Nonadaptive polynomial lower bounds are already known; the question explicitly allows each probe to depend on earlier contents. The intended cost is an amortized operation bound, including randomized structures with bounded error.

     References:
     Brody and Larsen, Adapt or Die: Polynomial Lower Bounds for Non-Adaptive Dynamic Data Structures (2015), https://cs.au.dk/~larsen/papers/adaptordie.pdf
     Larsen, Weinstein and Yu, Crossing the Logarithmic Barrier for Dynamic Boolean Data Structure Lower Bounds (2018/2020), https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.03575
description: Exhibit an explicit dynamic Boolean data-structure problem with O(log n)-bit operation arguments for which every polynomial-space adaptive cell-probe structure, with Θ(log n)-bit cells, requires n^{Ω(1)} update or query cost. Achieving such an unconditional bound would go far beyond Larsen’s polylogarithmic lower bounds without restricting adaptivity.

author: Ce Jin
title: Nearly linear approximate counting for knapsack
text:
Can the number of subsets of n nonnegative integer weights whose sum is at most a given capacity be estimated within 1±ε, with constant success probability, in Õ(n·poly(1/ε)) time? Feng and Jin’s randomized subquadratic counting algorithm leaves this natural input-linear target open.

     Remark: The target uses the usual arithmetic/word-operation model, suppressing logarithmic dependence on encoded weights and capacity. An October 2026 deterministic improvement still does not attain this target: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14595

     References:
     Feng and Jin, Approximately Counting Knapsack Solutions in Subquadratic Time (2024/2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.22267
description: Can the number of subsets of n nonnegative integer weights whose sum is at most a given capacity be estimated within 1±ε, with constant success probability, in Õ(n·poly(1/ε)) time? Feng and Jin’s randomized subquadratic counting algorithm leaves this natural input-linear target open.

author: Soheil Behnezhad
title: A one-pass approximation scheme for random-order streaming matching
text:
Can a single-pass algorithm find a (1−ε)-approximate maximum matching, for every fixed ε>0, using O_ε(n·polylog n) space when graph edges arrive in uniformly random order? Assadi and Behnezhad broke the 2/3 approximation barrier, but an approximation scheme remains a substantial open target.

     Remark: This editorial target concerns random-order insertion-only streams, not adversarial-order or insertion/deletion streams.

     References:
     Assadi and Behnezhad, Beating Two-Thirds For Random-Order Streaming Matching (2021), https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.07011
description: Can a single-pass algorithm find a (1−ε)-approximate maximum matching, for every fixed ε>0, using O_ε(n·polylog n) space when graph edges arrive in uniformly random order? Assadi and Behnezhad broke the 2/3 approximation barrier, but an approximation scheme remains a substantial open target.

author: Neal E. Young
title: Computing optimal generalized binary split trees
text:
Is there a polynomial-time algorithm for an optimal generalized binary split tree, where each node first tests equality against one key and otherwise branches using a potentially different split key? The objective is minimum expected search depth for given probabilities of successful queries.

     Remark: The claimed 1984 polynomial-time algorithm was shown incorrect by these authors. Polynomial algorithms for ordinary two-way comparison search trees do not settle this distinct model.

     References:
     Chrobak, Golin, Munro and Young, On Huang and Wong’s algorithm for generalized binary split trees (2022), https://doi.org/10.1007/s00236-021-00411-z
description: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm for an optimal generalized binary split tree, where each node first tests equality against one key and otherwise branches using a potentially different split key? The objective is minimum expected search depth for given probabilities of successful queries.

author: Sunil Arya
title: Instance-optimal outer approximation of convex polytopes
text:
For fixed dimension d, can one efficiently construct an outer polytope P with K⊆P⊆K+εB whose number of facets is within a dimension-dependent constant factor of the minimum possible for that particular input polytope K and error ε? Arya and Mount explicitly distinguish this instance-optimal goal from their achieved volume-sensitive worst-case bounds.

     References:
     Arya and Mount, Optimal Volume-Sensitive Bounds for Polytope Approximation, Discrete & Computational Geometry 74 (2025). https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00454-025-00780-z
description: For fixed dimension d, can one efficiently construct an outer polytope P with K⊆P⊆K+εB whose number of facets is within a dimension-dependent constant factor of the minimum possible for that particular input polytope K and error ε? Arya and Mount explicitly distinguish this instance-optimal goal from their achieved volume-sensitive worst-case bounds.

author: Sunil Arya
title: Optimal space–query tradeoff for approximate Voronoi diagrams
text:
For n sites in fixed-dimensional Euclidean space, determine the optimal worst-case size of a (t,ε)-approximate Voronoi diagram: a subdivision into quadtree boxes or differences of boxes, each storing at most t sites, one of which is a (1+ε)-nearest neighbour for every query in that cell. The issue is the full tradeoff between storage and t, rather than a bound at just one endpoint.

     Remark: Model qualification: this asks about the geometric size of the restricted representative-based AVD, not the best unrestricted nearest-neighbour data structure. Arya, da Fonseca and Mount’s 2017 polytope-membership methods already improve unrestricted approximate nearest-neighbour space bounds. https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.01696

     References:
     Arya, Malamatos and Mount, Space-time tradeoffs for approximate nearest neighbor searching, JACM 57 (2009). https://doi.org/10.1145/1613676.1613677
     Author manuscript. https://cse.hkust.edu.hk/~arya/pub/avd-ann.pdf
description: For n sites in fixed-dimensional Euclidean space, determine the optimal worst-case size of a (t,ε)-approximate Voronoi diagram: a subdivision into quadtree boxes or differences of boxes, each storing at most t sites, one of which is a (1+ε)-nearest neighbour for every query in that cell. The issue is the full tradeoff between storage and t, rather than a bound at just one endpoint.

author: Andrei Z. Broder
title: Exact uniform spanning-tree sampling in linear time
text:
Can an exactly uniform random spanning tree of any connected unweighted undirected graph be generated in expected O(m) time in the standard word-RAM model? Broder’s random-walk sampler launched this line of work, and subsequent almost-linear algorithms do not attain the literal linear-time target.

     References:
     A. Z. Broder, Generating Random Spanning Trees, FOCS 1989: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs/user/glmiller/public/Scientific-Computing/F-11/RelatedWork/Broder-GenRanSpanningTrees.pdf
     A. Schild, An Almost-Linear Time Algorithm for Uniform Random Spanning Tree Generation, STOC 2018: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.06455
description: Can an exactly uniform random spanning tree of any connected unweighted undirected graph be generated in expected O(m) time in the standard word-RAM model? Broder’s random-walk sampler launched this line of work, and subsequent almost-linear algorithms do not attain the literal linear-time target.

author: Friedrich Otto
title: The Madlener–Otto plain-group conjecture
text:
Must every group admitting a finite confluent length-reducing string-rewriting presentation be a free product of finitely many finite groups and a finitely generated free group? This asks exactly which groups have word problems solvable by this particularly simple finite normalization mechanism.

     References:
     K. Madlener and F. Otto, Groups presented by certain classes of finite length-reducing string-rewriting systems, TCS 65 (1989). https://doi.org/10.1016/0304-3975(89)90002-9
     M. Elder and A. Piggott, On groups presented by inverse-closed finite convergent length-reducing rewriting systems, 2021/2023. https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.03445
description: Must every group admitting a finite confluent length-reducing string-rewriting presentation be a free product of finitely many finite groups and a finitely generated free group? This asks exactly which groups have word problems solvable by this particularly simple finite normalization mechanism.

author: Alexander Okhotin
title: Complement closure of conjunctive languages
text:
Is the complement of every language generated by a conjunctive grammar itself generated by a conjunctive grammar? This asks whether conjunction and ordinary grammar recursion can express negation without adding the explicit negation operator of Boolean grammars.

     References:
     A. Okhotin, Conjunctive and Boolean grammars: The true general case of the context-free grammars, Computer Science Review 2013: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S157401371300018X
     O. Martynova and A. Okhotin, Non-closure under complementation for unambiguous linear grammars, Information and Computation 2023: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0890540123000329
description: Is the complement of every language generated by a conjunctive grammar itself generated by a conjunctive grammar? This asks whether conjunction and ordinary grammar recursion can express negation without adding the explicit negation operator of Boolean grammars.

author: Alexander Okhotin
title: A Greibach normal form for conjunctive grammars
text:
Can every conjunctive language not containing the empty word be generated with rules A→aβ₁ & ⋯ & aβₖ, where each βᵢ is a string of nonterminals? Such a normal form would ensure that each recursive expansion consumes an input symbol, generalizing a fundamental theorem for context-free grammars.

     References:
     A. Okhotin, Hardest languages for conjunctive and Boolean grammars, Information and Computation 2019: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0890540118301585
     S. Kuznetsov, Conjunctive Grammars in Greibach Normal Form and the Lambek Calculus with Additive Connectives, Formal Grammar 2013: https://www.mi-ras.ru/~sk/wissenschaft/conjGreibach.pdf
description: Can every conjunctive language not containing the empty word be generated with rules A→aβ₁ & ⋯ & aβₖ, where each βᵢ is a string of nonterminals? Such a normal form would ensure that each recursive expansion consumes an input symbol, generalizing a fundamental theorem for context-free grammars.

author: Francine Blanchet-Sadri
title: Deciding pattern avoidance over a prescribed alphabet
text:
Given a finite pattern p whose symbols are variables and an integer k≥2, is there an algorithm deciding whether some infinite k-letter word avoids every nonerasing substitution instance of p? Decidability when the alphabet size is unrestricted is known; fixing its size is the unresolved issue explicitly discussed in Blanchet-Sadri’s pattern research.

     References:
     F. Blanchet-Sadri and A. Lohr, Computing Depths of Patterns, RAIRO-ITA50 (2016), Section1: https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1051/ita/2016014.pdf
description: Given a finite pattern p whose symbols are variables and an integer k≥2, is there an algorithm deciding whether some infinite k-letter word avoids every nonerasing substitution instance of p? Decidability when the alphabet size is unrestricted is known; fixing its size is the unresolved issue explicitly discussed in Blanchet-Sadri’s pattern research.

author: Enrico Formenti
title: Dense periodic behavior in surjective one-dimensional cellular automata
text:
Must every surjective cellular automaton on the full two-sided one-dimensional shift have a dense set of temporally periodic configurations? Equivalently, must every finite prescribed block occur in some configuration that returns to itself after finitely many updates?

     References:
     L. Acerbi, A. Dennunzio and E. Formenti, Conservation of some dynamical properties for operations on cellular automata, TCS410 (2009): https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tcs.2009.05.004
description: Must every surjective cellular automaton on the full two-sided one-dimensional shift have a dense set of temporally periodic configurations? Equivalently, must every finite prescribed block occur in some configuration that returns to itself after finitely many updates?

author: Markus Holzer
title: Does nondeterminism add power with two two-way heads?
text:
Is there a language recognized by a nondeterministic two-way finite automaton with two input heads that no deterministic two-way finite automaton with two heads recognizes? This asks about recognition power with unrestricted finite control, rather than the number of states needed for a simulation.

     Remark: The equality of these two language classes would imply L=NL; the known strict hierarchy obtained by adding more heads does not settle this comparison.

     References:
     M. Holzer, M. Kutrib and A. Malcher, Multi-Head Finite Automata: Characterizations, Concepts and Open Problems, EPTCS1 (2009): https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.3051
description: Is there a language recognized by a nondeterministic two-way finite automaton with two input heads that no deterministic two-way finite automaton with two heads recognizes? This asks about recognition power with unrestricted finite control, rather than the number of states needed for a simulation.

author: Joachim Niehren
title: Is general context unification in NP?
text:
Can solvability of finite equations between trees containing ordinary variables and one-hole context variables be certified in polynomial size and verified in polynomial time? This is an editorial extension of Niehren and coauthors’ NP result for well-nested context unification to unrestricted instances.

     Remark: Decidability itself was settled by Jeż; the remaining question is the sharper complexity bound.

     References:
     J. Levy, J. Niehren and M. Villaret, Well-Nested Context Unification, CADE2005: https://doi.org/10.1007/11532231_11
     A. Jeż, Context Unification is in PSPACE, ICALP2014: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.4367
description: Can solvability of finite equations between trees containing ordinary variables and one-hole context variables be certified in polynomial size and verified in polynomial time? This is an editorial extension of Niehren and coauthors’ NP result for well-nested context unification to unrestricted instances.

author: Sanjay Jain
title: Isomorphism of tree-automatic ordinals without addition
text:
Is there an algorithm deciding whether two promised well-orders presented by finite-tree automata are isomorphic, when only their domains and order relations are supplied? Jain and coauthors solve the version with an automatic ordinal-addition operation, leaving this weaker presentation open.

     References:
     S. Jain, B. Khoussainov, P. Schlicht and F. Stephan, The isomorphism problem for tree-automatic ordinals with addition, Information Processing Letters 149 (2019): https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.13153
description: Is there an algorithm deciding whether two promised well-orders presented by finite-tree automata are isomorphic, when only their domains and order relations are supplied? Jain and coauthors solve the version with an automatic ordinal-addition operation, leaving this weaker presentation open.

author: Oscar H. Ibarra
title: Complement closure of deterministic finite-testable counter languages
text:
Are languages accepted by one-way deterministic finite-testable multicounter machines closed under complement? Here each counter has a fixed bound on successful zero-tests along accepting computations, and the input has a right end marker.

     References:
     Ibarra and McQuillan, On the containment problem for deterministic multicounter machine models, Information and Computation 307 (2025), 105383, §8. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ic.2025.105383 ; author manuscript: https://harvest.usask.ca/bitstreams/a74ef7ae-9bb7-4e83-893d-5751686076c1/download
description: Are languages accepted by one-way deterministic finite-testable multicounter machines closed under complement? Here each counter has a fixed bound on successful zero-tests along accepting computations, and the input has a right end marker.

author: Oscar H. Ibarra
title: Complementing unambiguous partially blind counter languages
text:
Is the complement of every language accepted by an unambiguous one-way partially blind multicounter machine accepted by some nondeterministic partially blind multicounter machine? Equivalently, ask this for unambiguous finite-testable multicounter machines; the output machine need not remain unambiguous.

     References:
     Ibarra and McQuillan, On the containment problem for deterministic multicounter machine models, Information and Computation 307 (2025), 105383, §8. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ic.2025.105383 ; author manuscript: https://harvest.usask.ca/bitstreams/a74ef7ae-9bb7-4e83-893d-5751686076c1/download
description: Is the complement of every language accepted by an unambiguous one-way partially blind multicounter machine accepted by some nondeterministic partially blind multicounter machine? Equivalently, ask this for unambiguous finite-testable multicounter machines; the output machine need not remain unambiguous.

author: Johann A. Makowsky
title: Fagin’s binary-relation spectrum problem
text:
Can every first-order spectrum be represented by a sentence whose vocabulary consists of just one binary relation? The set of finite-model sizes must be preserved exactly, so encodings that merely rescale the sizes do not settle the question.

     References:
     A. Durand, N. D. Jones, J. A. Makowsky and M. More, Fifty Years of the Spectrum Problem: Survey and New Results, Bulletin of Symbolic Logic 2012, Open Question 4: https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.5495
description: Can every first-order spectrum be represented by a sentence whose vocabulary consists of just one binary relation? The set of finite-model sizes must be preserved exactly, so encodings that merely rescale the sizes do not settle the question.

author: Matthias Baaz
title: Craig interpolation for Gödel logic with function symbols
text:
Does first-order Gödel logic with truth values [0,1], allowing function symbols and without built-in equality, have Craig interpolation? Whenever A entails B, the desired interpolant I must use only their common nonlogical symbols and satisfy A entails I and I entails B.

     Remark: The relational-language case, with constants but no function symbols, was settled positively before the cutoff; the cited paper explicitly leaves this extension open.

     References:
     J. P. Aguilera and M. Baaz, Ten problems in Gödel logic (2017), Problem2: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00500-016-2366-9
     S. M. A. Khatami, M. Pourmahdian and N. R. Tavana, The Craig Interpolation Property in First-order Gödel Logic (2023/2024), Section4: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10860
description: Does first-order Gödel logic with truth values [0,1], allowing function symbols and without built-in equality, have Craig interpolation? Whenever A entails B, the desired interpolant I must use only their common nonlogical symbols and satisfy A entails I and I entails B.

author: Matthias Baaz
title: Effective prenex normalization for countable Gödel truth-value sets
text:
For which countably infinite closed truth-value sets V⊆[0,1] containing 0 and 1 is there an effective transformation taking every first-order formula to a prenex formula that is valid in G_V exactly when the original is valid? This asks for preservation of validity, rather than logical equivalence, and seeks to complete Baaz–Gamsakhurdia’s classification.

     Remark: The case V={1−1/(n+1):n≥0}∪{1}, and the corresponding finite-valued cases, already admit such normalization.

     References:
     M. Baaz and M. Gamsakhurdia, Goedel logics: Prenex fragments (2024): https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16683
description: For which countably infinite closed truth-value sets V⊆[0,1] containing 0 and 1 is there an effective transformation taking every first-order formula to a prenex formula that is valid in G_V exactly when the original is valid? This asks for preservation of validity, rather than logical equivalence, and seeks to complete Baaz–Gamsakhurdia’s classification.

author: Alexander Moshe Rabinovich
title: Deciding MSO-definable choice on the infinite binary tree
text:
Given a monadic second-order formula φ(X,Y) over the full infinite binary tree, is it decidable whether an MSO-definable function selects exactly one valid Y for each X for which any valid Y exists? Rabinovich proves positive uniformization results for finite cross-sections, but unrestricted relations remain the target.

     References:
     A. Rabinovich, On Uniformization in the Full Binary Tree, MFCS2022: https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.MFCS.2022.77
description: Given a monadic second-order formula φ(X,Y) over the full infinite binary tree, is it decidable whether an MSO-definable function selects exactly one valid Y for each X for which any valid Y exists? Rabinovich proves positive uniformization results for finite cross-sections, but unrestricted relations remain the target.

author: Alexander Moshe Rabinovich
title: Continuous-time synthesis for Metric Interval Temporal Logic
text:
Is the Church synthesis problem decidable for MITL specifications over finitely variable signals on the nonnegative real line? Given a specification relating input and output signals, determine whether a causal operator can satisfy it for every input, with output at time t depending only on input up to t.

     Remark: The authors settle MSO order specifications, not MITL’s metric constraints; this is their signal-operator synthesis model, rather than a differently parameterized timed-game model.

     References:
     A. Rabinovich and D. Fattal, The Church Synthesis Problem over Continuous Time, LMCS2025, Section7: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.04782
description: Is the Church synthesis problem decidable for MITL specifications over finitely variable signals on the nonnegative real line? Given a specification relating input and output signals, determine whether a causal operator can satisfy it for every input, with output at time t depending only on input up to t.

author: Hans Kleine Büning
title: Recognizing minimally false quantified formulas of fixed deficiency
text:
For each fixed k≥2, determine the complexity of recognizing closed prenex CNF quantified Boolean formulas that are false but become true after deletion of any clause, when the number of clauses minus the number of existential variables is k. Kleine Büning’s problem asks whether these restricted minimal-falsity tests have polynomial algorithms or remain computationally hard.

     Remark: Deficiency1 is already polynomial-time decidable; the fixed-k problem is known to lie in DP.

     References:
     H. Kleine Büning and X. Zhao, Computational complexity of quantified Boolean formulas with fixed maximal deficiency, TCS407 (2008): https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tcs.2008.07.022
     H. Kleine Büning, Open Problems for Quantified Boolean Formulas, QBF2016, slide7: https://fmv.jku.at/qbf16/HKB-QBF16.pdf
description: For each fixed k≥2, determine the complexity of recognizing closed prenex CNF quantified Boolean formulas that are false but become true after deletion of any clause, when the number of clauses minus the number of existential variables is k. Kleine Büning’s problem asks whether these restricted minimal-falsity tests have polynomial algorithms or remain computationally hard.

author: Hans Kleine Büning
title: Near-linear equivalence testing for propositional Horn theories
text:
Can equivalence of two propositional Horn CNF formulas be decided in O(N log N), or even O(N), time, where N is their combined number of literal occurrences? This would improve the quadratic general algorithm while preserving the ability to compare complete sets of logical consequences.

     References:
     H. Kleine Büning, Open Problems for Quantified Boolean Formulas, QBF2016, slides12–13: https://fmv.jku.at/qbf16/HKB-QBF16.pdf
description: Can equivalence of two propositional Horn CNF formulas be decided in O(N log N), or even O(N), time, where N is their combined number of literal occurrences? This would improve the quadratic general algorithm while preserving the ability to compare complete sets of logical consequences.

author: Yuri Gurevich
title: An effective syntax for order-invariant first-order queries
text:
Is there an effectively presented logic defining exactly the queries expressible by first-order formulas with an auxiliary linear order whose choice does not affect the result? This is an editorial continuation of Gurevich’s work showing that order-invariant first-order logic can express more than ordinary first-order logic.

     References:
     Y. Gurevich, Logic and the Challenge of Computer Science (1988): https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/logic-challenge-computer-science/
     N. Schweikardt, A tutorial on order-invariant logics (2015): https://www2.informatik.hu-berlin.de/~schweikn/downloads/Schweikardt_Slides_TutorialOnOrderInvariantLogics_SLS-SummerSchool-2015.pdf
     F. Harwath, On invariant formulae of first-order logic with numerical predicates, dissertation (2017), Introduction: https://edoc.hu-berlin.de/server/api/core/bitstreams/0a7a8533-e8a8-47df-942d-28f6c775db26/content
description: Is there an effectively presented logic defining exactly the queries expressible by first-order formulas with an auxiliary linear order whose choice does not affect the result? This is an editorial continuation of Gurevich’s work showing that order-invariant first-order logic can express more than ordinary first-order logic.

author: Thomas A. Henzinger
title: Polynomial-time quantitative stochastic parity verification
text:
Can the threshold winning probability in finite turn-based stochastic parity games be computed in polynomial time, with both the number of priorities and binary-encoded rational probabilities unrestricted? This is the quantitative verification problem studied directly by Henzinger, Chatterjee and Jurdziński, combining adversarial control, randomness and infinite-run specifications.

     References:
     K. Chatterjee, M. Jurdziński and T. A. Henzinger, Simple Stochastic Parity Games, CSL2003: https://ptolemy.berkeley.edu/projects/chess/pubs/729.html
description: Can the threshold winning probability in finite turn-based stochastic parity games be computed in polynomial time, with both the number of priorities and binary-encoded rational probabilities unrestricted? This is the quantitative verification problem studied directly by Henzinger, Chatterjee and Jurdziński, combining adversarial control, randomness and infinite-run specifications.

author: Claudia Faggian
title: A probabilistic Newman lemma with ordinary local confluence
text:
For a probabilistic abstract rewrite system, do almost-sure termination under every reduction strategy and ordinary local confluence of the lifted multidistribution relation imply a unique limiting distribution on normal forms? Faggian explicitly leaves AST+WCR⇒UN∞ open; merely requiring branches to join at the limit is insufficient.

     References:
     C. Faggian, Probabilistic Rewriting and Asymptotic Behaviour: on Termination and Unique Normal Forms, LMCS18(2),2022, Remark4.7: https://lmcs.episciences.org/9386
description: For a probabilistic abstract rewrite system, do almost-sure termination under every reduction strategy and ordinary local confluence of the lifted multidistribution relation imply a unique limiting distribution on normal forms? Faggian explicitly leaves AST+WCR⇒UN∞ open; merely requiring branches to join at the limit is insufficient.

author: Claudia Faggian
title: Fully abstract game semantics for pure call-by-value
text:
Construct a compositional game model for the pure untyped call-by-value lambda calculus in which denotational equality coincides exactly with contextual equivalence, observed through termination in all closing contexts. This is the pure-calculus full-abstraction target in Faggian’s research programme, distinct from existing models for typed languages or languages extended with state and control.

     References:
     B. Accattoli, A. Lancelot and C. Faggian, Normal Form Bisimulations By Value (2023): https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08161
     A. Kerinec, G. Manzonetto and S. Ronchi Della Rocca, Call-By-Value, Again!, FSCD2021: https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.FSCD.2021.7
     B. Accattoli and C. Faggian, Values, Games, and Costs, doctoral research proposal for Adrienne Lancelot: https://www.irif.fr/_media/users/lancelot/thesis_subject_adrienne.pdf
description: Construct a compositional game model for the pure untyped call-by-value lambda calculus in which denotational equality coincides exactly with contextual equivalence, observed through termination in all closing contexts. This is the pure-calculus full-abstraction target in Faggian’s research programme, distinct from existing models for typed languages or languages extended with state and control.

author: Dexter Kozen
title: A finite algebraic axiomatization of full guarded KAT
text:
Does full guarded Kleene algebra with tests admit a finite sound and complete algebraic inference system for its guarded-string language equivalence? In particular, determine whether the infinitary uniqueness axiom can be derived from the remaining finite axioms, rather than assuming a rule for arbitrary systems of equations.

     References:
     S. Smolka, N. Foster, J. Hsu, T. Kappé, D. Kozen and A. Silva, Guarded Kleene Algebra with Tests: Verification of Uninterpreted Programs in Nearly Linear Time, POPL2020: https://doi.org/10.1145/3371129
     J. Rot, T. Schmid and J. Wagemaker, GKAT with Hoare Hypotheses, CONCUR2026, §2 records the remaining question: https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CONCUR.2026.46
description: Does full guarded Kleene algebra with tests admit a finite sound and complete algebraic inference system for its guarded-string language equivalence? In particular, determine whether the infinitary uniqueness axiom can be derived from the remaining finite axioms, rather than assuming a rule for arbitrary systems of equations.

author: Dale Miller
title: Cut elimination for classical fixed-point arithmetic μLK_p⁺
text:
Does every proof in Manighetti–Miller’s μLK_p⁺ admit a cut-free proof of the same sequent? The system adds unrestricted weakening and contraction to first-order μMALL with equality and least/greatest fixed points; consistency and an embedding of Peano arithmetic are known, but eliminating intermediate lemmas remains open.

     References:
     M. Manighetti and D. Miller, Peano Arithmetic and μMALL, Fundamenta Informaticae 194 (2025): https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13634v3
description: Does every proof in Manighetti–Miller’s μLK_p⁺ admit a cut-free proof of the same sequent? The system adds unrestricted weakening and contraction to first-order μMALL with equality and least/greatest fixed points; consistency and an embedding of Peano arithmetic are known, but eliminating intermediate lemmas remains open.

author: Jean Goubault-Larrecq
title: Commutativity of the full probabilistic powerdomain monad
text:
Is the monad of all continuous valuations on dcpos commutative: can the order of two independent probabilistic computations always be exchanged? Goubault-Larrecq’s semantics obtains this property for minimal valuations, but the full continuous-valuation monad remains the open target.

     References:
     J. Goubault-Larrecq, Is there any trouble with the probabilistic powerdomain monad?, research talk (2024): https://topology.lmf.cnrs.fr/is-there-any-trouble-with-the-probabilistic-powerdomain-monad/
     J. Goubault-Larrecq and X. Jia, Separating minimal valuations, point-continuous valuations, and continuous valuations (2021): https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.00426
description: Is the monad of all continuous valuations on dcpos commutative: can the order of two independent probabilistic computations always be exchanged? Goubault-Larrecq’s semantics obtains this property for minimal valuations, but the full continuous-valuation monad remains the open target.

author: Nicole Schweikardt
title: Eliminating an invariant order on bounded-degree structures
text:
On every class of finite relational structures of bounded Gaifman degree, is each order-invariant first-order sentence equivalent to an ordinary first-order sentence? This asks whether an arbitrary auxiliary order adds any expressive power even on locally sparse structures, continuing Schweikardt’s work on invariant logics.

     Remark: Later partial progress: the 2026 result proves collapse for the cluster-FO fragment, leaving unrestricted order-invariant FO as the broader target.

     References:
     N. Schweikardt, A Short Tutorial on Order-Invariant First-Order Logic, CSR 2013: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-38536-0_10
     N. Schweikardt, A tutorial on order- and arb-invariant logics, research slides, final open questions: https://www.irif.fr/~steiner/jifp/schweikardt.pdf
     F. Ghasemi and J. Grange, Order-Invariant Cluster First-Order Logic on Graph Classes of Bounded Degree, MFCS 2026: https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.MFCS.2026.71
description: On every class of finite relational structures of bounded Gaifman degree, is each order-invariant first-order sentence equivalent to an ordinary first-order sentence? This asks whether an arbitrary auxiliary order adds any expressive power even on locally sparse structures, continuing Schweikardt’s work on invariant logics.

author: Jean-François Raskin
title: Decidability of the infinite target discounted-sum problem
text:
Given rational numbers 0<λ<1 and a,b,t, decide whether an infinite sequence wᵢ∈{a,b} satisfies Σᵢ≥0wᵢλⁱ=t. This is the arithmetic obstruction studied in Raskin’s work on rational verification of discounted-sum games.

     Remark: The finite-word version and special discount factors are decidable. The September 2026 probabilistic Markov-chain result concerns a different variant and does not settle this existence question: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03670 .

     References:
     Brice, Raskin and van den Bogaard, Rational Verification for Nash and Subgame-Perfect Equilibria in Graph Games, MFCS 2023, Problem 12. https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.MFCS.2023.26
     Boker, Henzinger and Otop, The Target Discounted-Sum Problem, LICS 2015; expanded 2025 version. https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.22979
description: Given rational numbers 0<λ<1 and a,b,t, decide whether an infinite sequence wᵢ∈{a,b} satisfies Σᵢ≥0wᵢλⁱ=t. This is the arithmetic obstruction studied in Raskin’s work on rational verification of discounted-sum games.

author: Orna Kupferman
title: Decidability of the nondeterministic tree-automaton index problem
text:
Given a nondeterministic parity automaton on infinite binary trees and a finite priority interval J, decide whether an equivalent nondeterministic automaton using only priorities in J exists. This is an editorial continuation of Kupferman and Vardi’s work on transformations between acceptance conditions and tree-automaton emptiness.

     References:
     Kupferman and Vardi, Weak alternating automata and tree automata emptiness, STOC 1998. https://doi.org/10.1145/276698.276748
     Idir and Lehtinen, Using Games and Universal Trees to Characterise the Nondeterministic Index of Tree Languages, ICALP 2025. https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.160
description: Given a nondeterministic parity automaton on infinite binary trees and a finite priority interval J, decide whether an equivalent nondeterministic automaton using only priorities in J exists. This is an editorial continuation of Kupferman and Vardi’s work on transformations between acceptance conditions and tree-automaton emptiness.

author: Emanuel Kieronski
title: Satisfiability with two variables and one transitive relation
text:
Is satisfiability decidable for first-order logic using only two variables when one designated binary relation must be transitive and the remaining relations are unrestricted? The question permits infinite models and continues Kieroński’s work on semantic restrictions in two-variable logic.

     Remark: Finite satisfiability is already decidable (Pratt-Hartmann, 2018); it must not be conflated with this unrestricted satisfiability question: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.05558.

     References:
     Kieroński, Pratt-Hartmann and Tendera, Two-variable logics with counting and semantic constraints, SIGLOG News 5(3), 2018, https://doi.org/10.1145/3242953.3242958
     On two-variable first-order logic with a partial order, Journal of Logic and Computation 36(2), 2026, https://academic.oup.com/logcom/article/36/2/exaf068/8442300
description: Is satisfiability decidable for first-order logic using only two variables when one designated binary relation must be transitive and the remaining relations are unrestricted? The question permits infinite models and continues Kieroński’s work on semantic restrictions in two-variable logic.

author: Emanuel Kieronski
title: Decidability of the full alternating uniform one-dimensional fragment
text:
Is satisfiability decidable for the equality-free fragment AUF1, allowing arbitrary alternation inside quantifier blocks while retaining uniformity and at most one free variable after each block? Fiuk and Kieroński settle important restricted blocks and the three-variable subfragment, but leave the full fragment open.

     References:
     Fiuk and Kieroński, Alternating Quantifiers in Uniform One-Dimensional Fragments with an Excursion into Three-Variable Logic, LMCS 21(1), 2025, §6, https://lmcs.episciences.org/15387/pdf
description: Is satisfiability decidable for the equality-free fragment AUF1, allowing arbitrary alternation inside quantifier blocks while retaining uniformity and at most one free variable after each block? Fiuk and Kieroński settle important restricted blocks and the three-variable subfragment, but leave the full fragment open.

author: Delia Kesner
title: A perpetual reduction strategy for the λσ calculus
text:
Construct an effective perpetual reduction strategy for the full λσ explicit-substitution calculus: whenever a term admits an infinite reduction, the strategy must itself produce an infinite reduction. Kesner explicitly identifies this problem in studying safe and fully compositional substitution calculi.

     References:
     Kesner, A Theory of Explicit Substitutions with Safe and Full Composition, LMCS 5(3), 2009, concluding discussion, https://www.irif.fr/~kesner/papers/safe-full-composition.pdf
description: Construct an effective perpetual reduction strategy for the full λσ explicit-substitution calculus: whenever a term admits an infinite reduction, the strategy must itself produce an infinite reduction. Kesner explicitly identifies this problem in studying safe and fully compositional substitution calculi.

author: Alexis Saurin
title: Uniform cut elimination with digging and fixed points
text:
Extend the uniform cut-elimination theorem for μsuperLL∞ to include digging rules, which permit nested exponential modalities, while retaining least and greatest fixed points and the validity condition for non-wellfounded proofs. Bauer and Saurin identify digging as the missing case in their general theorem; suitable explicit restrictions may be necessary.

     References:
     Bauer and Saurin, A uniform cut-elimination theorem for linear logics with fixed points and super exponentials (2025), §6, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.14327v1
description: Extend the uniform cut-elimination theorem for μsuperLL∞ to include digging rules, which permit nested exponential modalities, while retaining least and greatest fixed points and the validity condition for non-wellfounded proofs. Bauer and Saurin identify digging as the missing case in their general theorem; suitable explicit restrictions may be necessary.

author: Thomas Schwentick
title: Can quantifier-free updates maintain directed reachability?
text:
Is directed reachability maintainable under single-edge insertions and deletions by quantifier-free update formulas with a fixed finite collection of auxiliary relations of arbitrary fixed arity (DynProp)? Schwentick’s question is about unrestricted relational auxiliary arity, beyond known lower bounds for bounded-arity subclasses.

     Remark: First-order updates with quantifiers already maintain directed reachability (2015); that result does not settle DynProp.

     References:
     Schwentick, An Open Question in Dynamic Descriptive Complexity (2017), https://databasetheory.org/sites/default/files/blog_attach/SchwentickOpenProblems_0.pdf
     Zeume and Schwentick, On the quantifier-free dynamic complexity of Reachability (2015), https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ic.2014.09.011
description: Is directed reachability maintainable under single-edge insertions and deletions by quantifier-free update formulas with a fixed finite collection of auxiliary relations of arbitrary fixed arity (DynProp)? Schwentick’s question is about unrestricted relational auxiliary arity, beyond known lower bounds for bounded-arity subclasses.

author: Thomas Schwentick
title: A polynomial-time query outside DynFO
text:
Exhibit a polynomial-time computable Boolean query on finite relational structures that cannot be maintained by first-order update formulas under single-tuple insertions and deletions, even with arbitrary fixed-arity auxiliary relations. This is the central lower-bound frontier emphasized by Schwentick, using the standard empty-input initialization and allowing built-in arithmetic.

     References:
     Schwentick and Zeume, Dynamic Complexity: Recent Updates (2016), https://informatik-rub.de/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/SchwentickZ2016-siglog.pdf
     Schwentick, An Open Question in Dynamic Descriptive Complexity (2017), https://databasetheory.org/sites/default/files/blog_attach/SchwentickOpenProblems_0.pdf
description: Exhibit a polynomial-time computable Boolean query on finite relational structures that cannot be maintained by first-order update formulas under single-tuple insertions and deletions, even with arbitrary fixed-arity auxiliary relations. This is the central lower-bound frontier emphasized by Schwentick, using the standard empty-input initialization and allowing built-in arithmetic.

author: Robert Weismantel
title: Polynomial-time integer programming with bounded subdeterminants
text:
For every fixed Δ, can arbitrary integer linear programs min{cᵀx:Ax≤b, x∈ℤⁿ} be solved in polynomial time when every square subdeterminant of the integer matrix A has absolute value at most Δ? Weismantel and coauthors’ bimodular algorithm handles Δ≤2; the question allows zero determinants and unrestricted row sparsity.

     References:
     S. Artmann, R. Weismantel and R. Zenklusen, A Strongly Polynomial Algorithm for Bimodular Integer Linear Programming, STOC 2017: https://doi.org/10.1145/3055399.3055473
     S. Fiorini, G. Joret, S. Weltge and Y. Yuditsky, Integer Programs with Bounded Subdeterminants and Two Nonzeros per Row, FOCS 2021/JACM 2025: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.05947
description: For every fixed Δ, can arbitrary integer linear programs min{cᵀx:Ax≤b, x∈ℤⁿ} be solved in polynomial time when every square subdeterminant of the integer matrix A has absolute value at most Δ? Weismantel and coauthors’ bimodular algorithm handles Δ≤2; the question allows zero determinants and unrestricted row sparsity.

author: Robert Weismantel
title: A linear bound in the flatness theorem
text:
Is the lattice width of every convex body in ℝⁿ whose interior contains no integer point at most Cn for a universal constant C? Here lattice width is the minimum, over nonzero integer vectors a, of maxₓaᵀx−minₓaᵀx; a linear bound would sharpen a basic geometric ingredient of integer programming.

     Remark: This is a broader geometric target extending the authors’ flatness bounds for polyhedra; the known near-linear bound does not establish O(n).

     References:
     M. Celaya, S. Kuhlmann, J. Paat and R. Weismantel, Proximity and Flatness Bounds for Linear Integer Optimization, Mathematics of Operations Research 2024: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.14941
     V. Reis and T. Rothvoss, The Subspace Flatness Conjecture and Faster Integer Programming, FOCS 2023: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.14605
description: Is the lattice width of every convex body in ℝⁿ whose interior contains no integer point at most Cn for a universal constant C? Here lattice width is the minimum, over nonzero integer vectors a, of maxₓaᵀx−minₓaᵀx; a linear bound would sharpen a basic geometric ingredient of integer programming.

author: Michele Conforti
title: Polynomial-size split closures in fixed dimension
text:
For each fixed dimension d≥3, does the split closure of a rational polyhedron admit an inequality description polynomial in the binary length of the original description? The split closure intersects all cuts obtained from integer disjunctions a·x≤b or a·x≥b+1; this extends Conforti and collaborators’ positive planar result.

     Remark: Dimension2 is already settled; polynomial-time integer optimization in fixed dimension does not by itself bound the size of this particular closure.

     References:
     A. Basu, M. Conforti, M. Di Summa and H. Jiang, Split cuts in the plane, SIAM Journal on Optimization31 (2021): https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.05022
description: For each fixed dimension d≥3, does the split closure of a rational polyhedron admit an inequality description polynomial in the binary length of the original description? The split closure intersects all cuts obtained from integer disjunctions a·x≤b or a·x≥b+1; this extends Conforti and collaborators’ positive planar result.

author: Amitabh Basu
title: Oertel’s mixed-integer centerpoint conjecture
text:
For a convex body C in R^{n+d}, must C∩(Z^n×R^d) contain a point such that every closed halfspace containing it captures at least 1/(2^n e) of the total mixed-integer volume? Volume here sums d-dimensional volumes over integer fibers; the conjecture controls progress guarantees for mixed-integer cutting-plane optimization.

     Remark: The 2026 paper strengthens sufficient thickness conditions but explicitly leaves the unrestricted conjecture open.

     References:
     A. Basu and T. Oertel, Centerpoints: A link between optimization and convex geometry, SIOPT27 (2017): https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.08609
     H. Cheng and A. Basu, Linear Threshold for Oertel’s Conjecture on the Mixed-Integer Volume (2026): https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00286
description: For a convex body C in R^{n+d}, must C∩(Z^n×R^d) contain a point such that every closed halfspace containing it captures at least 1/(2^n e) of the total mixed-integer volume? Volume here sums d-dimensional volumes over integer fibers; the conjecture controls progress guarantees for mixed-integer cutting-plane optimization.

author: Bertrand Guenin
title: Seymour’s dyadic packing conjecture
text:
For every ideal clutter and nonnegative integral element capacities, does the dual of its minimum-weight covering LP have an optimal packing whose coordinates are dyadic rationals, with denominators powers of 2? This asks whether integrality of the covering polyhedron forces a uniform arithmetic structure on optimal fractional packings.

     Remark: The 2025 dyadic-packing theorem for dijoins settles a special case, not all ideal clutters; the 2026 local-dyadic work also treats a weaker conjecture and special cases. See Guenin’s publication list: https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/~bguenin/papers.html.

     References:
     B. Guenin and L. Tunçel, Generalizations of Total Dual Integrality (2025): https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07925
description: For every ideal clutter and nonnegative integral element capacities, does the dual of its minimum-weight covering LP have an optimal packing whose coordinates are dyadic rationals, with denominators powers of 2? This asks whether integrality of the covering polyhedron forces a uniform arithmetic structure on optimal fractional packings.

author: Bertrand Guenin
title: The Flowing conjecture for ideal binary clutters
text:
Is every binary clutter ideal exactly when it has none of the three forbidden minors: the Fano-plane line clutter, the odd-circuit clutter of K5, and the blocker of the latter? Equivalently, are these the only minimally nonideal binary clutters, giving a complete structural criterion for integral covering.

     References:
     G. Cornuéjols and B. Guenin, Ideal Binary Clutters, Connectivity, and a Conjecture of Seymour, SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics15(2002): https://doi.org/10.1137/S0895480100371389
     B. Guenin, Integer covering problems, statement of the Flowing conjecture: https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/~bguenin/covering.html
description: Is every binary clutter ideal exactly when it has none of the three forbidden minors: the Fano-plane line clutter, the odd-circuit clutter of K5, and the blocker of the latter? Equivalently, are these the only minimally nonideal binary clutters, giving a complete structural criterion for integral covering.

author: Volker Kaibel
title: Explicit matroids with exponentially large extended formulations
text:
Construct an explicit family of matroids on n elements whose base polytopes require 2^{Ω(n)} inequalities in every linear extended formulation. Counting proves such matroids exist, but does not identify a concrete family.

     Remark: Editorial continuation of Kaibel’s work on compact formulations for structured matroid classes; the 2025 paper explicitly records the contrasting explicit-family question as open.

     References:
     Conforti, Kaibel, Walter and Weltge, Subgraph polytopes and independence polytopes of count matroids (2015): https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S016763771500084X
     Ferroni and Schröter, Face enumeration for split matroid polytopes (2025): https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548325000021
description: Construct an explicit family of matroids on n elements whose base polytopes require 2^{Ω(n)} inequalities in every linear extended formulation. Counting proves such matroids exist, but does not identify a concrete family.

author: Daniel Bienstock
title: A polynomial-size constant-gap relaxation for minimum knapsack
text:
Does every minimum-knapsack covering instance admit an objective-independent extended linear relaxation of polynomial size with a universal constant integrality gap for all nonnegative costs? This continues Bienstock’s study of knapsack inequalities; known quasi-polynomial-size constant-gap formulations do not settle it.

     References:
     Bienstock et al., On inequalities with bounded coefficients and pitch for the min knapsack polytope, Discrete Optimization (2021), https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disopt.2020.100567
     Bazzi, Fiorini, Huang and Svensson, Small Extended Formulation for Knapsack Cover Inequalities from Monotone Circuits, Theory of Computing 14 (2018), https://toc.cs.uchicago.edu/articles/v014a014/v014a014.pdf
description: Does every minimum-knapsack covering instance admit an objective-independent extended linear relaxation of polynomial size with a universal constant integrality gap for all nonnegative costs? This continues Bienstock’s study of knapsack inequalities; known quasi-polynomial-size constant-gap formulations do not settle it.

author: Daniel Bienstock
title: A fully polynomial-size LP relaxation scheme for maximum knapsack
text:
Can maximum 0–1 knapsack be approximated simultaneously for every nonnegative profit vector by an objective-independent extended LP of size polynomial in n and 1/ε with gap at most 1+ε? Bienstock’s polynomial-size schemes for each fixed ε leave this stronger analogue of an FPTAS unresolved.

     References:
     Bienstock, Approximate formulations for 0–1 knapsack sets, Operations Research Letters (2008), https://doi.org/10.1016/j.orl.2007.09.003
     Faenza and Sanità, On the existence of compact ε-approximated formulations for knapsack in the original space (2015), https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.04717
description: Can maximum 0–1 knapsack be approximated simultaneously for every nonnegative profit vector by an objective-independent extended LP of size polynomial in n and 1/ε with gap at most 1+ε? Bienstock’s polynomial-size schemes for each fixed ε leave this stronger analogue of an FPTAS unresolved.

author: Alexander Rakhlin
title: Characterizing agnostic online reinforcement learning
text:
Which finite policy classes Π permit learning an ε-optimal member in every unknown horizon-H MDP using only poly(H, log|Π|, 1/ε) online episodes, for a fixed finite action set? Rakhlin and collaborators showed that bounded spanning capacity suffices with a generative model but not online; a necessary-and-sufficient characterization is missing.

     References:
     Jia, Li, Rakhlin, Sekhari and Srebro, When is Agnostic Reinforcement Learning Statistically Tractable?, NeurIPS (2023): https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06113
     Publisher version of the same paper: https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/58a799d16fb0c1f2014e98f4ba972b25-Abstract-Conference.html
description: Which finite policy classes Π permit learning an ε-optimal member in every unknown horizon-H MDP using only poly(H, log|Π|, 1/ε) online episodes, for a fixed finite action set? Rakhlin and collaborators showed that bounded spanning capacity suffices with a generative model but not online; a necessary-and-sufficient characterization is missing.

author: Ilias Diakonikolas
title: Polynomial-time proper learning of Poisson binomial distributions
text:
From samples of an unknown sum of n independent Bernoulli variables, can one learn to total-variation error ε in time polynomial in 1/ε and log n while outputting a Poisson binomial distribution, represented by distinct parameters and their multiplicities? The hypothesis need not recover the original Bernoulli parameters.

     Remark: The cited algorithm has (1/ε)^{O(log log(1/ε))} dependence; non-proper learning is already polynomial-time.

     References:
     Diakonikolas, Kane and Stewart, Properly Learning Poisson Binomial Distributions in Almost Polynomial Time, COLT 2016: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v49/diakonikolas16b.html
description: From samples of an unknown sum of n independent Bernoulli variables, can one learn to total-variation error ε in time polynomial in 1/ε and log n while outputting a Poisson binomial distribution, represented by distinct parameters and their multiplicities? The hypothesis need not recover the original Bernoulli parameters.

author: Sanjay Jain
title: Does extra automatic memory beyond the longest example help learning?
text:
If an automatic family of languages is identifiable in the limit from positive examples by an automatic learner with unrestricted memory, must it also be learnable when its memory length is bounded by the longest example seen, up to an additive constant? The learner must succeed on every text enumerating the target language; equivalent automatic hypothesis codings may be chosen.

     Remark: This is the positive-data-only model. With arbitrary negative counterexamples, longest-example-sized memory is already sufficient for every automatic family.

     References:
     Jain, Kinber and Stephan, Automatic Learning from Positive Data and Negative Counterexamples, Information and Computation 255 (2017), introduction: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ic.2017.05.002
